Array.name: TAKE

Lambda.name: LAMBDA
Lambda.label: Lambda
Lambda.description: Creates a custom, reusable function. Use it inline (call it immediately) or store it as a Named formula to call it by name. The last argument is the body; the previous ones are the parameters. Trailing parameters may be omitted at call time (use ISOMITTED); optional parameters can be written as [name] in the definition.

arguments.name: parameters, calculation
arguments.description: Comma-separated parameter names followed by the calculation body, e.g. x, x+1 or n, [currency], ...

Lambda.name: LET
Lambda.label: Let
Lambda.description: Assigns names to intermediate results, then uses them in a final calculation. Names are computed once, improving readability and performance.

arguments.name: names, values, calculation
arguments.description: Alternating name/value pairs, ending with the calculation that uses them

Lambda.name: MAP
Lambda.label: Map
Lambda.description: Applies a LAMBDA to each element of one or more arrays (element-wise) and returns an array of the results. The LAMBDA must take one parameter per array.

arguments.name: array1, [array2, ...]
arguments.description: One or more ranges/arrays of the same shape

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.description: A LAMBDA(...) or a named lambda applied to each element

Lambda.name: REDUCE
Lambda.label: Reduce
Lambda.description: Reduces an array to a single accumulated value by applying a LAMBDA(accumulator, value) to each element in turn.

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.description: LAMBDA(accumulator, value) returning the new accumulator

Lambda.name: SCAN
Lambda.label: Scan
Lambda.description: Like REDUCE, but returns the array of every intermediate accumulator value (running totals).

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.description: LAMBDA(accumulator, value) returning the new accumulator

Lambda.name: BYROW
Lambda.label: ByRow
Lambda.description: Applies a LAMBDA to each row of an array and returns a column of results. The LAMBDA receives the row as an array.

Lambda.name: BYCOL
Lambda.label: ByCol
Lambda.description: Applies a LAMBDA to each column of an array and returns a row of results. The LAMBDA receives the column as an array.

Lambda.name: MAKEARRAY
Lambda.label: MakeArray
Lambda.description: Returns a calculated array of the given size by applying a LAMBDA(row, col) with 1-based indices.

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.description: LAMBDA(row, col) returning each cell value

notes.variableArguments: Functions with -1 as argumentCount accept a variable number of arguments. Examples: SUM(), COUNT(), CONCAT(), AND(), OR()
notes.conditionalCriteria: Functions COUNTIF, SUMIF, AVERAGEIF and their variants accept different types of criteria: exact value ("Apple" or 10), numeric comparison (">10", "<5", ">=100", "<=50"), wildcards ("*text*" contains, "text*" starts with, "*text" ends with, "?" single character)
notes.volatileFunctions: Some functions are marked as volatile and are automatically recalculated: ROW() recalculated on row changes, COLUMN() recalculated on column changes, ROWS() recalculated on row changes, COLUMNS() recalculated on column changes, RAND(), RANDBETWEEN() and INDIRECT() recalculated on every change
notes.dataTypes: Functions accept numeric values, text strings, dates, cell references, and ranges. Ranges can be specified as A1:A10 or A1:C10. Cell references can be absolute ($A$1) or relative (A1)
notes.lambda: LAMBDA can be used two ways: inline in a cell (e.g. =LAMBDA(x, x+1)(5) or as the argument of MAP/REDUCE/SCAN), or stored as a Named formula (right panel > Named formulas) to call it by name (e.g. SURFACE = LAMBDA(l, h, l*h) then =SURFACE(3, 4)). A named LAMBDA can call itself (recursion). An inline LAMBDA can capture outer variables from an enclosing LET (closures). A LAMBDA value bound in LET can be called like a function (e.g. LET(f, LAMBDA(x, x+1), f(3))). Trailing parameters may be omitted; ISOMITTED detects missing optional arguments (definition may use [name]).
